domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
summary: Microsoft Foundry organizes AI work into hubs (shared resources, governance, and connections) and projects (team workspaces) that inherit from them.
highYield: Know the hub vs project distinction: hubs centralize resources, security, and connections; projects are where teams build and inherit from the hub.
Know what connections are and why they are used instead of hard-coded secrets.
Know that tracing records each step of an agent/application for debugging and that evaluation scores groundedness, relevance, coherence, and fluency.
Know the six responsible AI principles: fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency, and accountability.
memoryAids: Six responsible AI principles: 'FRPITA' — Fairness, Reliability and safety, Privacy and security, Inclusiveness, Transparency, Accountability.
Hub vs project: 'Hub Holds, Projects Play' — the hub holds shared resources; projects are where you build.
Connections = 'reusable secret holders': remember they centralize credentials so projects never hard-code keys.

domain: Implement generative AI and agentic solutions
summary: Generative AI solutions combine models with grounding (RAG), tool use (function calling), and agents (tools, knowledge, memory, MCP), tuned via settings like temperature and validated by evaluation.
highYield: RAG = retrieve relevant chunks and inject them into the prompt to ground answers; embeddings power the vector similarity search.
Function calling returns a structured request the app uses to call an API, then sends results back to the model.
Low temperature = deterministic/factual; high temperature = creative/varied.
Agent building blocks: tools (actions), knowledge (grounding data), memory (conversation state), and MCP (portable tool connectivity standard).
memoryAids: RAG: 'Retrieve And Ground' — you retrieve docs and ground the answer in them.
Temperature = 'how creative': turn it down for facts, up for brainstorming.
Agent anatomy 'T-K-M-M': Tools, Knowledge, Memory, MCP.

summary: Azure AI Vision and related services analyze images (tags, captions, objects), read text (OCR), detect faces, and let you train custom classifiers and detectors.
highYield: Image Analysis returns captions, tags, and detected objects from a single call.
OCR (Read API) extracts printed and handwritten text from images and PDFs.
Azure AI Face detects faces and attributes and can compare or identify faces, but it is gated by limited-access policy.
Custom Vision trains custom image classification and object detection from labeled images without deep-learning code.
memoryAids: 'Analyze, Read, Face, Custom' — the four vision pillars.
Custom Vision = 'your data, your labels, no deep learning code'.
Face is restricted: remember 'limited access' applies to identification scenarios.

summary: Azure AI Language offers prebuilt text capabilities (sentiment, key phrases, entities, PII, summarization, question answering) while Azure AI Translator handles translation.
highYield: Sentiment analysis returns positive/negative/neutral polarity; opinion mining adds aspect-level detail.
Key phrase extraction returns the main noun phrases; NER returns typed entities (person, location, organization).
PII detection finds and can redact personal data such as names, phone numbers, and ID numbers.
Custom question answering answers FAQ/document questions with confidence scores, no model training from scratch.
memoryAids: 'S K E P' — Sentiment, Key phrases, Entities, PII are the four core prebuilt text features.
PII = 'Protect It Immediately': use it to redact before you store or publish.

summary: Azure AI Document Intelligence extracts structured data from documents using prebuilt models for common types or custom models you train on your own forms.
highYield: Prebuilt models (invoice, receipt, ID document, layout, read) work with no training.
Custom template models suit fixed layouts; custom neural models handle varied layouts.
Read/layout models extract text and structure (tables, selection marks) from documents.
Choose prebuilt first when a document type matches an existing model; choose custom for bespoke forms.
memoryAids: Prebuilt vs custom: 'prebuilt = plug and play, custom = teach it your form'.
Template = fixed layout; Neural = flexible layout.
Document Intelligence (formerly Form Recognizer): same service, extraction of fields and tables.
